title: Guest Posting SEO: goals, qualifying sites, pitching, and avoiding penalties
summary: Jacky Chou's beginner guide to guest posting as an SEO and growth tactic. It covers setting goals, finding and qualifying sites, pitching, writing, tracking results, and spammy practices that risk Google penalties.

principles.text: Set a clear goal for each guest post (leads, sales, backlinks, traffic, awareness). Not every post has to be only about links.
principles.quote: not every guest blog post must solely focus on obtaining backlinks.

principles.text: Qualify guest post sites: real traffic, good authority, quality content, and not built just to sell links.
principles.quote: The site should be created for more than just accepting guest posts. If every published post has outbound links to random websites, it was most likely designed to sell links.

principles.text: Find opportunities by copying competitors' backlinks, contacting influencers, and using search operators.
principles.quote: Checking the competitors’ backlinks and trying to secure guest posts on the same sites

principles.text: Customize each pitch to the site and say how the owner and readers benefit and how you'll promote the post.
principles.quote: Your guest post is more likely to be accepted if your pitch is well-crafted and customized to the site.

principles.text: Keep links few and relevant: one author-bio link, a few contextual links, natural anchor text, no keyword stuffing.
principles.quote: Including a half-dozen backlinks in the main body of the guest blog post is another sign that you are attempting to manipulate it.

principles.text: Track traffic, leads, authority and rankings from each guest post, then use the data to improve the next one.
principles.quote: By monitoring these metrics, you can assess your guest blogging campaign’s effectiveness and make adjustments.
